project.visitorDecision: Choose a Hattie Cove day hike and understand exactly which mapped path-to-road or path-to-path relationships are source-backed, without confusing them with legal signed trailhead access.
project.primaryAction: Inspect the original shared OSM node evidence for the selected day hike, then check the illustrated Parks Canada route map and latest park access reports before visiting.

claims.subject: route-guidance
claims.limitation: Park-return hiking descriptions and named routes do not supply verified signed GPS junction coordinates or present access.

claims.subject: parking-rule
claims.limitation: Visitor Centre parking is the published arrival area but opening and navigable access from the lot are not verified by this document.

claims.subject: route-guidance
claims.limitation: Exact OSM shared node membership is supported; the source cannot establish signed trailhead, hiking permission, complete route, vertex GPS survey or safety.

claims.subject: park-access
claims.limitation: Both official trail FeatureServer layers returned zero paths intersecting the Hattie Cove envelope; missing geometry is not a park access restriction or permission.

claims.subject: park-access
claims.accessScope: White River Suspension Bridge Trail only, officially reported closed October 22, 2026
claims.limitation: The last reported closure blocks selection; an older positive report for other trails does not establish current access.

decisionState.selectedIdField: Existing Pukaskwa chooser selectedTrail id via pukaskwa:choice event
decisionState.sourceOfTruth: Parks Canada official visitor route reference remains authoritative for hiking; static OSM junction evidence module supplies only exact source relationships, never permission or opening.
decisionState.unavailableBehavior: Source GIS, OSM way lines or tiles missing: retain official map and static source explanation, and never infer a parking-to-footway route.

scenarios.input: Two hours, moderate, Lake Superior coast; default Southern Headland
scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: Selected headland remains the primary hike with two independently recorded OSM junction relationships and an explicit no-signed-start notice.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: Parks Canada lists the Visitor Centre origin; OSM node membership is not a signed or legally accessible trail entrance.

scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: Boardwalk Beach becomes selected; evidence changes to the recorded South Loop and Beach Trail shared nodes with original OSM source links.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: Adjacent OSM service-road geometry does not establish an approved walk to the beach or safe access.

scenarios.input: Southern Headland to Boardwalk Beach and back to Southern Headland
scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: Junction records return to the correct original headland node IDs and selected hiking title without stale Boardwalk links.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: Reversible evidence selection does not override a park closure or status freshness checks.

scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: Static Southern Headland shared-node source links, separate official route starting guidance and original park map remain readable.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: No GPS route generated without scripts; original sources and uncertainty survive.

scenarios.input: CARTO and OSM map tiles both blocked
scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: Original illustrated Parks Canada map and the source evidence panel remain available without a blank map or false navigation advice.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: Community node membership never becomes a new route line.

scenarios.input: Official October 12 open observations and October 22 bridge closure on November 1
scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: Hikes carry stale/unknown current access labels and bridge remains closed regardless of nearby mapped way nodes.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: Updated collector timestamp is not a new issued trail observation.

scenarios.expectedVisibleAnswer: Panel says no reviewed mapped entrance junction and keeps original park route description.
scenarios.sourceAndSafety: Named multi-trail circuit is not a complete surveyed coordinate graph.

failures.no-js: Show the original Parks Canada illustrated map and two static headland OSM shared-node citations; keep the explicit parking-to-path uncertainty in HTML.
failures.no-tiles: Switch to the Parks Canada illustrated map with existing seven GIS visitor-place links; shared-node provenance stays text-only.
failures.no-image: Keep full hiking chooser, source-backed start explanation and original node links, with no dependency on photos to understand access.
failures.stale-data: Keep old official open records stale, preserve explicit White River closure and never use the fresh OSM audit date to imply fresh park status.

qa.scopeNote: Exact-head Chromium actually loaded raster tiles and 7 agency GIS pins plus 14 OSM trail segments at 360/390/768/1366/1440 px. Checked A-B-A selection, native details, source failure, both tile providers failing, and no-JavaScript. Inspected phone390 and desktop1440 screenshot evidence from run artifact 13082649265. No separate production interactive click test or visitor-outcome measurement is claimed.

verificationLimit: Source-only structural check does not certify signed trailheads, park access or route navigation. Browser QA was exact-head Chromium, and independent public smoke verified heading, default OSM way records, route warning, original park map, canonical and v4 module. No production interaction or engagement measurement.
